claims.text: The initial microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can preserve or inherit the microstructural lamellae.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing that inherits lamellae will reduce microcracking.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing that inherits lamellae will enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
Reduced microcracking and enhanced grain-boundary cohesion will improve tensile strength.
Reduced microcracking and enhanced grain-boundary cohesion will improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
Designed microstructural architectures will produce enhanced strength-ductility synergy.
The intervention will increase tensile strength by 20% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The intervention will increase tensile ductility by 30% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The predicted improvements apply during room-temperature tensile deformation.
The hypothesis is bounded to processing temperatures from 800°C to 1000°C.
The hypothesis is bounded to strain rates from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^-1 s^-1.
The exact processing parameters and resulting microstructural features depend on alloy composition and processing history.
An increase of less than 10% in both tensile strength and tensile ductility relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
